items.line: Serebii.net, a Pokémon news site, says Pokémon UNITE will reach end of service on March 23, 2027, on both mobile and Nintendo Switch. A second post says the game will then enter a library mode, for viewing what players own and for Practice Mode.
PopCrave, a pop culture account, says Noah Wyle has been named People Magazine's Sexiest Man Alive for 2026. Not checked here.
Fox News reports, in a 27-second video post, that the FBI has raided a Beverly Hills mansion as part of an investigation into Eric Swalwell. The post gives no further detail. Not checked here.

NFL reporter Adam Schefter says, with Ian Rapoport, that the Colts have agreed to trade guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks. He says Nelson is on an expiring contract and the Colts want draft picks back before he can leave in free agency.

Google DeepMind says Genie 4 is its most realistic and interactive world model yet, one where people in a scene move, react and speak in real time. Sundar Pichai, Google's chief executive, says it is rolling out as a research preview to trusted testers.

Melania Trump's account posts that a ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 27, two days early, and says General Valery Gerasimov has confirmed it. Not checked here.

Fabrizio Romano, a football transfer reporter, says Manchester United have decided to keep Michael Carrick as head coach despite the defeats to Bournemouth and Como. He says Carrick will be in charge for Saturday's match against Chelsea. Not checked here.

Dexerto, a gaming and entertainment news outlet, says Discord will soon make public server messages searchable on Google. It says the feature will be on by default for US adults, who can opt out in their privacy settings. Not checked here.

The account PlaystationSize says Grand Theft Auto VI will be a 210 GB download, with a $79.99 standard edition, pre-load from November 12 and release at midnight on November 19. Other accounts repeat it as the PS5 size. Not checked here.

Eric Daugh posts words he attributes to US Ambassador Mike Waltz at the UN, telling a Cuban official to "sit down" and saying "This isn't Havana". Daugh says the official tried to intimidate Waltz. The attached post carries a video of the exchange. What happened in the room is not checked here.
Barack Obama posts that it is one week to Election Day and urges Ohio voters to vote early or make a plan for November 3rd. He names Sherrod Brown and Amy Acton as the candidates he backs there.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio posts a map image with the words "Private island of corrupt regime in Cuba". The post gives no further detail. It is part of the US-Cuba exchange at the UN. Not checked here.
Sky Sports Football posts a 40-second video and says Arsenal’s Max Dowman has been shown a red card. A second post says it was against Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup.

Fleetwood Town, the League Two club, posts that it has knocked Arsenal out of the League Cup. A second post, from football reporter Fabrizio Romano, says Arsenal were eliminated from the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood.

Senator Bernie Sanders lists what he says has happened since Trump's election, including that Elon Musk became the first trillionaire, and says Musk is spending $442 million to keep Republicans in control of Congress. Not checked here.

Commentator Candace Owens says she was personally dismissed from the lawsuit French President Emmanuel Macron filed against her in Delaware. She says reporters misdescribed what the suit was about and gives her own account of it. Not checked here.
Shah Rukh Khan, the actor, posts a photo and a line in Hindi, in Latin letters, for his film KING, which he says opens in cinemas on 24 December 2026.

A user posts that Benjamin Netanyahu has officially lost the Israeli election and asks Grok to confirm it. Grok is made by xAI, the company behind the model that gathers the posts on this page. The claim is not checked here.
ShowCaseShabazz posts a 10-second video captioned "TATUM CALLS GAME". ESPN NBA, in the attached post, says Jayson Tatum hit a game-winner against the Nets. Not checked here.
Pop Base, an entertainment news account, posts that Noah Wyle has been named People magazine's Sexiest Man Alive of 2026.

Elon Musk posts a link announcing new features in Grok @Bot. The video it quotes, from matt palmer, lists them: pages, a vault, 1Password and Apple integrations, video making, new bot characters and X Spaces. Musk owns xAI, which makes Grok, the model that gathers this page's posts.
A post asks whether someone in prison who gets sleepy around 1 p.m. is allowed to take a nap. It is a question, and the post gives no answer.

Uday, a coder, tells Microsoft his idea for layoffs: search YouTube for "Day in the life of a Microsoft Engineer" and lay off the people who he says only eat and do not work in the office. It is his view of the videos; Microsoft is not heard in the post. Not checked here.
NBA reporter Shams Charania says, citing sources to ESPN, that Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards will have an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee and miss up to two months.

Open Source Intel, a news-sharing account, says at least 46 are dead and 179 injured after an Iryo train and a Renfe train collided near Toledo, Spain. These are the post's figures; Spanish outlets were still revising theirs. Not checked here.
Rep. Joaquin Castro says that losing an election is not grounds for asylum, and that the Trump administration is giving Flavio Bolsonaro safe haven. Not checked here.

The Washington Post reports that a Brazilian Supreme Court justice has ordered a police investigation into alleged ties between a donor network co-founded by Vice President JD Vance and Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, ahead of Sunday’s election. Not checked here.

Shay Boloor, a markets commentator, posts a chart image and a list of figures he says are SoFi’s third-quarter results and its guidance for the next two years, against analyst estimates. The figures are his; not checked here.

India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, says elections for MLC seats were held in 28 seats across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka, using ballot papers. He asks how many seats Congress won and does not give the result in the post. Not checked here.

Sam McDowell, a reporter for The Kansas City Star, says the Chiefs are signing kicker Justin Tucker to the practice squad, citing a source. ESPN’s Adam Schefter repeats it and adds that Tucker has not kicked in the NFL since 2024, after a personal-conduct violation following allegations of sexual misconduct.
MLB posts a 12-second video captioned “Ben Williamson walk-off, Rays survive.” Reporter Jeff Passan says the Rays beat the Brewers 4-3 in 12 innings after trailing, so the World Series continues.

Artificial Analysis, an AI benchmarking firm, announces version 5 of its Intelligence Index. It says Claude Opus 5.5 leads, ahead of two OpenAI models, and that Anthropic and OpenAI hold the top five places. These are its results and are not checked here. Claude, the model writing this page, is made by Anthropic.
